title: How Microsoft 365 & Copilot Are Redesigning the Way We Work with Tracy van der Schyff [MVP]
description:
Many organizations switch on Copilot and expect it to fix a chaotic Microsoft 365 environment. In this conversation, Mirko Peters and Tracy van der Schyff discuss digital fluency, the Me, We, Us model, ontological design and permanent change management for adoption leads, IT managers and business leaders. You will learn why investing in people matters more than adding another tool.
In this episode
00:00 – Introduction and Tracy's path into the Microsoft ecosystem02:09 – From PC literacy to digital fluency04:00 – Where work belongs: the Me, We, Us model11:30 – What changed when Copilot entered the workplace19:20 – Ontological design: what we create shapes us23:40 – Teams, noise and using AI to overcome fear of AI35:50 – Copilot in a broken digital workplace and change management59:30 – Rapid-fire round and closing
Key takeaways
Digital fluency goes beyond knowing which buttons to click: people need to use tools with purpose, efficiently and responsibly, and that now includes AI.Copilot does not fix a messy Microsoft 365 environment; it amplifies what is already there, so storage habits, sharing and permissions have to be addressed first.Change management works only as a permanent part of the company's strategy, explaining to people why practices matter rather than just telling them what to do.
Worth quoting
“I think in the era of AI, the responsible use of technology is going to become the most important thing, apart from all the skills that we should focus on.” – Tracy van der Schyff (03:44)
“And whether it's co-pilot or whatever it might be, as I mentioned, it doesn't fix things, okay, it amplifies. So, if you had a healthy environment, it's going to amplify that healthy environment.” – Tracy van der Schyff (37:46)
